counterevidence_considered.description: The only candidate source of dependence is that all 24 colonies were sampled from a single ridge during one field season, so the choices could share environmental context. This is a spatial/temporal clustering caveat, not a repeated entry of an independent unit into the procedure, and the description asserts outcrops were at least fifty metres apart with no repeated testing; it therefore does not demonstrate the target issue class.

source_refs.quoted_text:
This table records a nest-choice survey of the rock ant Temnothorax rugatulus
carried out along one ridge during a single field season. Twenty-four
queenright colonies were located, each living under a different granite
outcrop, and no two sampled outcrops were closer than fifty metres. Each
colony was lifted intact into a plaster arena offering two identical cavities,
one shaded by a dark filter and one left open to ambient light, and was scored
once for the cavity into which it completed its emigration. After scoring, the
colony was returned to its outcrop and was never tested again.

evidence.description: All 24 values of the declared independent-unit column colony_id (TR-01 through TR-24) are distinct in data/input.csv; no colony contributes more than one row to the binomial count.

The data description states the independent unit is colony_id, that one row is one colony scored once, and that every colony label appears on exactly one row with each outcrop supplying exactly one colony.

source_refs.quoted_text:
- colony_id: the label of the colony; every label appears on exactly one row.
- collection_outcrop: the granite outcrop the colony was taken from; every
  outcrop supplied exactly one colony.

One row is: one field-collected ant colony scored once in a single two-cavity nest-choice trial
Independent unit column: colony_id
One trial is: one row

evidence.description: The workflow actively enforces one row per independent unit before the row-independent binomial test: it raises a ValueError if any colony_id or collection_outcrop value repeats, so repeated unit entry cannot silently reach the test.

The reported result matches an independent recount of the raw rows: 19 of 24 rows have cavity_chosen = shaded (exposed rows are TR-03, TR-07, TR-12, TR-17, TR-22), and the exact two-sided binomial p-value for 19/24 against 0.5 is 0.00661 as reported, so the tested count is a count of distinct colonies.

source_refs.quoted_text:
- Colonies assayed: 24
- Emigrated to the shaded cavity: 19
- Emigrated to the exposed cavity: 5
- Observed proportion choosing shaded: 0.7917
- Null proportion: 0.5
- Exact two-sided p-value: 0.00661

[selected-result] Exact two-sided binomial test on 24 independent colonies: 19 of 24 (proportion 0.7917) chose the shaded cavity against a null of 0.5, p = 0.00661, so the no-preference null is rejected at alpha = 0.05.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by searching for any independent unit entering the binomial test more than once: I enumerated all 24 colony_id values in data/input.csv and confirmed each appears exactly once, checked collection_outcrop for hidden nesting (multiple colonies per outcrop) and found all 24 outcrop labels distinct, and traced the workflow to confirm the test statistic is built from one outcome per row with duplicate colony_id or outcrop rows rejected by explicit ValueError guards before the test runs. I also recounted shaded (19) and exposed (5) outcomes directly from the raw rows and verified they match the reported 19/24 with two-sided exact p = 0.00661, ruling out an inflated count from repeated unit entry. No route by which a unit could enter the procedure repeatedly survived these checks.
